summary:
Space Mind is an application designed to support and protect astronauts' mental health during their space journeys and missions. Its main goal is to promote the emotional and psychological well-being of people who face the physical and mental challenges of living and working beyond Earth.

The application focuses on several important aspects, including space psychology, stress management, anxiety, isolation, loneliness, and the emotional challenges that may arise during space missions. It also aims to provide tools to strengthen emotional stability, concentration, and the ability to adapt to extreme environments.

Additionally, Space Mind includes an interactive chatbot that allows astronauts to communicate, express their emotions, share their concerns, and receive guidance and emotional support. In this way, the app provides a safe space for communication and assistance that astronauts can access throughout their time in space.

Ultimately, Space Mind aims to ensure that astronauts are not only physically and technically prepared for space travel, but also emotionally and psychologically prepared, recognizing that mental health is an essential part of the success of every space mission.
details:
Space Mind is a mobile application designed to support astronauts' mental health and emotional well-being during space travel and missions. Living and working in space can create psychological challenges such as stress, anxiety, loneliness, isolation, and emotional difficulties. Our project aims to address these challenges by providing astronauts with tools and support to take care of their mental health.

The application focuses on different aspects of space psychology, emotional well-being, stress management, and psychological adaptation to life beyond Earth. One of its main features is an interactive chatbot, which allows users to have conversations, express their feelings, share their concerns, and receive emotional support and guidance.

The main benefit of Space Mind is that it helps astronauts understand and manage their emotions while facing the unique challenges of space missions. Our goal is to make mental health care more accessible during space travel and contribute to healthier, safer, and more successful missions.

To develop our project, we used MIT App Inventor, a platform that allows us to design mobile applications and program their functions using visual block-based coding. We designed the interface and programmed the different features to create an application that can be used on mobile phones by anyone interested in astronaut psychology and space exploration.

Our team consists of six members, and we used two computers throughout the development process to design, program, and work on the project.

What makes Space Mind creative is its combination of space exploration and psychological well-being. While space missions usually focus on astronauts' physical and technical preparation, our project highlights the importance of their emotional and mental health. We considered factors such as isolation, stress, emotional stability, accessibility, and the difficulties of living far away from Earth.

Ultimately, we want Space Mind to demonstrate that taking care of astronauts' minds is just as important as preparing their bodies for space exploration.
